Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of Bangladesh's batting effort. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. A new opening pair for Bangladesh ​​​as Shadman Islam walks out to open the innings alongside Anamul Haque. Richard Ngarava will open the attack for Zimbabwe. Shadman will face the first ball. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go!
... SECOND INNINGS ...

As for Bangladesh, Taijul Islam was the standout performer with a six-wicket haul, well supported by Nayeem Hasan, who removed the two most experienced members of Zimbabwe’s batting lineup, Sean Williams and Craig Ervine. It is now up to their batting unit to build on the bowlers' fine effort and take control of the Test. Back in a bit for the hosts' reply with the bat.

A job well done by Bangladesh! It took them only one ball to wrap up the final wicket this morning. From a position of 161/2, Zimbabwe lost their last 8 wickets for just 66 runs in what turned out to be a dramatic collapse. Their top four batters all got starts, with Nick Welch and Sean Williams going on to register fifties, but the visitors needed much more and have fallen well short of the total they would have had in mind after winning the toss.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Excellent review from Bangladesh! Slower through the air, short in length, turning away, well outside off, Blessing Muzarabani pokes at it and the ball passes very close to the bat. The keeper, Jaker Ali, snaffles it cleanly. A loud appeal from Bangladesh's close-in fielders, but the on-field umpire is unmoved. Bangladesh decide to go for the review. Here's the third umpire on screen. UltraEdge shows a clear spike as the ball goes past the bat. The on-field call will be overturned and Zimbabwe have been bowled out for 227!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going on Day 2. Najmul Hossain Shanto leads his troops out to the centre. They are followed by Blessing Muzarabani and Tafadzwa Tsiga. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Taijul Islam. Taijul to Blessing. A slip and a silly point in place. Let's play...

As for Zimbabwe, they let a bright start slip away. Having been 161/2 at one stage after winning the toss, they had a golden opportunity to take control of the Test by piling on the runs. They will now be hoping this last pair can stretch the total as much as possible. Can the pair succeed in adding a few vital runs? Let's find out.

Spin was always expected to play a key role after pacers dominated proceedings in Sylhet and so it proved, with 7 of the 9 wickets falling to the spinners. Taijul Islam led the way, claiming his 16th Test five-wicket haul to run through the Zimbabwean batting lineup. Bangladesh will be eager to take this final wicket quickly and then get on with their reply with the bat.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second and final Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Chattogram. After an even first session and a second session that went the visitors' way, it was in the third session that the hosts scripted a remarkable turnaround to seize the ascendancy in the Test.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

After losing the toss at a venue where 500 has been crossed in the first innings in each of the last two Tests, Bangladesh will be delighted with the position they find themselves in. They will aim to wrap up the Zimbabwe innings quickly on Day 2 before turning their attention to building a strong reply with the bat. Tafadzwa Tsiga has shown stiff resistance during his 59-ball stay, and from a Zimbabwean perspective, much will rest on his shoulders to stretch the total further. The first ball on Day 2 will be bowled at 4 am GMT, but do join us early for the build-up. See you then. Cheers!

That proved to be just the opening Bangladesh needed, as Welch's departure brought a new batter to the crease, and the spinners quickly pounced on the opportunity. Nayeem Hasan and Taijul Islam combined brilliantly to chip away at the wickets, while a run out further compounded Zimbabwe’s troubles. Welch eventually returned at the fall of the 8th wicket but couldn’t add anything to the score and fell while trying to hit his way out of trouble.

Earlier in the day, Zimbabwe opted to bat first and made a steady start. Both Brian Bennett and Ben Curran put in the hard work, but fell to shots that could have been avoided. Sean Williams and Nick Welch then provided stability and went unscathed throughout the entire second session. The hot and humid conditions began to take a toll on Welch at the start of the third session, forcing him to retire hurt.

A remarkable turnaround by Bangladesh to claim the opening day honours! Zimbabwe began the third session in a position of strength at 161/2 but suffered a collapse of epic proportions. They lost 7 wickets for just 66 runs, leaving them to wonder what could have been after such a promising start.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the start of the third session. Bangladesh are in a huddle near the ropes. Nick Welch and Sean Williams make their way out to the middle. Mehidy Hasan Miraz will open the attack. Here we go!
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

This partnership is now worth 89 and Zimbabwe would hope for these two to continue the grind in the post-Tea session. There is turn on offer, but not threatening enough, and we have seen the odd ball staying low. Bangladeshi bowlers have to find some inspiration and try to break this partnership. The onus will be on their spinners till the new ball is available in the latter half of the third session. Back in a bit for the third and final session of the day.

There has been turn on offer, but the Zimbabwean batters weathered the spinners through their solid defence. In the first session, we saw Zimbabwe batters playing their shots, but in this session, they have respected the pitch and the opposition and have played the ball to its merit. In addition to that, they have also rotated the strike a fair bit, thereby rarely getting into a shell. Bangladeshi bowlers tried all they could, and there were some nervy moments for the batters here and there, but nonetheless, the batters remained untroubled.

End of session 2, and the players will feel a bit relieved as it has been very hot out there. Talking about the session, it’s been Zimbabwe all the way as they scored 72 runs in the session without losing a wicket, all thanks to Sean Williams and Nick Welch who have grinded it out in the middle. It’s not been easy by any means as the Bangladeshi spinners have been pretty much on the target, but the application shown by these two men has been commendable.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to begin. Najmul Hossain Shanto and his men make their way out to the middle. They are followed by the two openers of Zimbabwe, Brian Bennett and Ben Curran. Hasan Mahmud will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for the hosts. Let's play...

Before we get underway, a special presentation will take place. David Boon, the ICC match referee, is set to retire after this Test, and he is being honoured with a memento to mark his remarkable contribution to the game.

PITCH REPORT - Athar Ali Khan is near the deck. He says the wicket looks white in colour, and there is some grass but not like it was in Sylhet. Observes that there are cracks on the surface, which can be a concern later in this Test match. He believes this looks a good batting surface. Adds that there is a tinge of grass, but again, it shouldn’t be a concern over the course of this Test and as he said earlier this looks a great batting wicket. Feels that the captain winning the toss will look to bat first.

The skipper of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto says it looks like a pretty good wicket and mentions he does not mind batting second since the surface tends to play well even on Days 3 and 4. He hopes the batters are a bit more prepared this time and can produce something special.

The captain of Zimbabwe, Craig Ervine, says the surface looks drier and has less grass compared to what it was in Sylhet. He mentions it was a massive win in the first game, but stresses the need to refocus on this Test. He adds that little moments in the game are crucial, and admits Zimbabwe missed a few opportunities in Sylhet.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Anamul Haque (In for Mahmudul Hasan Joy), Shadman Islam, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Jaker Ali (WK), Taijul Islam, Hasan Mahmud, Nayeem Hasan (In for Khaled Ahmed), Tanzim Hasan Sakib (On debut) (In for Nahid Rana).
TOSS - Zimbabwe win the toss and they will BAT first.

Talking about the weather, rain is forecast for the first three days of the Test, with thunderstorms expected on Days 1 and 3. Fingers crossed the weather stays kind to us. Stick around for the toss and team news.

Zimbabwe, meanwhile, will be pleased with how their pace attack exploited the lively conditions in the first Test. However, their struggles against spin were evident in the second innings, and they will face a sterner examination here, with Bangladesh likely to prepare a pitch that assists spinners as the game progresses.

Bangladesh’s batting was their undoing in both innings of the first Test, and they will be keen to produce a much stronger showing here in Chattogram, where conditions are expected to be far more batting-friendly. However, they will be without Nahid Rana, who has left for the Pakistan Super League, leaving them without a genuine pace threat who could trouble batters with raw speed.

Hello and welcome to the opening day of the second Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe at the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium in Chattogram. The hosts face a quick turnaround as they look to level the two-match series, while Zimbabwe, buoyed by their first Test win since 2021, will be riding high on confidence.
